reviews.comment: Dr. Wilhite is low-key a total Gigachad of hyper-focus. Forget the chaos—this man's lectures are an absolute masterclass in precision. Every single minute of class is pure, unfiltered information!. He is incredibly kind and patient, but his laser-focused teaching style ensures you actually learn how to be a real engineer. Absolute legend. 10/10

Dr. Wilhite is a kind person who genuinely wants his students to learn, but his lecturing style can be a bit polarizing. He tends to ramble and go off on tangents during class, which can make it hard to follow the core engineering concepts. The workload is heavy and his grading is strict, so you have to stay focused.

Dr. Wilhite is a fair and dedicated professor. He teaches challenging engineering concepts but explains them clearly and responds thoroughly to questions. If you complete the assignments and participate in class, you will be well prepared for your upper-level coursework.

Pure tough love. Mass transport will humble you, but he's a total legend. Lectures are a wild mix of brutal math and hilarious, obscure jokes. He won't spoon-feed you, so expect zero sleep on exam weeks. Do the homework and use your brain. You'll leave exhausted but a real engineer. 10/10

Honestly, Wilhite is an absolute legend in the CHEN department. Is mass transport easy? Heck no, it's brutal, and he is a pretty tough grader. But he explains the fundamentals so well that everything actually clicks. He truly cares about preparing you for senior year and your actual career. Do the homework, go to office hours, and don't panic.

Professor can be tough on exam grading, but it pays off Senior Year - he may be acerbic at times and make obscure jokes in lecture, but he genuinely cares about you learning the material as it is so important for later classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor Wilhite really cares about making sure students know mass transport and mass transfer unit operations - it is critical to success in Senior year, and while this class may 'hurt' its worth it.
Wilhite is absolutely awesome.
great job!

Professor Wilhite is a great instructor - but you have to know going in that attending class is SOOO important! And the homeworks take some time, but if you can do them then you're trained up for acing the exams.
Dr. Wilhite drops science like Galileo dropped the orange!

The low ratings are misleading. His slides have mistakes, but they are easy to notice and he corrects them quickly. His practice exams are by far the best resource and very similar to the real exams. Homework is long and not very helpful. While TA review sessions carried, he grades fairly and gives partial credit, and is better than his rating.
He was boring and didn't made sense most of the time. Lectures are useless and didn't help at all.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Plss take someone else.

He makes mass transfer way harder than it should be. He doesn't show how to do problems and just uses his slides as guides for the lecture. He makes many mistakes in these slides and sometimes conflicts with the textbook. The homeworks are very difficult and half of the time it doesn't make any sense.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Wilhite is a very uninteresting professor. The lectures are often difficult to follow and concepts weren't explained clearly. The only thing he does is stand there and just go over the slides. The slides had many typos, making it hard to trust the material. The homework's were convoluted for no reason and didn't help in the exams.

This course was pretty easy. Wilhite provides slides that contain the necessary formulas and processes to solve the problems in the exams. The slides also contain examples that are similar to problems on the exam. He also gives a practice exam before each test. The slides have a few typos but they aren't that bad.

Would take someone else for Mass Transfer. He FLIES through lectures that have very crowded slides. Doesn't really do any good example problems. Weekly group homework that is extremely difficult. Practice exams are EASIER the real exams. Understand his lecture problems well.Content isn't that difficult, but Wilhite makes it harder.

He's not the most organized professor, but he's extremely smart and passionate. He's super friendly and approachable, so don't hesitate to ask him questions. His homework is pretty tough, but his exam reviews give you a good idea what to expect on his exams.

CHEN 324 during Spring Semester. Prof Wilhite provides good lectures. TA helped very much on the homeworks and exam prep. Practice exams provided were helpful to prepare for exams. 3 midterms for 20% each. Final exam was not cumulative and was 20%. Homework is 20%. Exam regrades are allowed. Prof Wilhite does well to convey difficult topics.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 4 exams. Lots of very difficult group hw. Lets you submit regrade requests because he takes a ton of points off at first. Lectures were full of mistakes and were not helpful. Very bad uninterested lecturer. TA carried the class with last minute exam reviews. Prof was pretty much useless and acted like he did not care. Seemed annoyed when questioned

Homeworks are done in groups. They're pretty hard and take a long time. 4 exams including the final, and each one's 20% of your grade. TA's review sessions for exams were super helpful. Dr. Wilhite offers exam corrections.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Homeworks are so difficult and take forever. He is horrible at lecturing and his slides have mistakes in them. He grades the exams super harshly and the exams were too long for the allotted time. If you have another option don't take him!!

This material is hard, but he makes it way harder to learn by going way to fast in class and not explaining anything in a way we could understand. Only talks about theory and derivations and does not explain how to go through problems, so no one knows how to do the homeworks. Definitely take a different professor.

Dr. Wilhite is very unorganized, he does not respond to emails, and he does not know how to teach this class. His lectures were above everyone's heads, and he was rarely accessible outside of class. He was not in office hours most of the time.

Lectures can be a little dry, but as long as you teach yourself the lecture slides, do the Hw, and understand the practice exams, you will be fine. You can go to his office hours with any questions. DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS AND UNDERSTAND THEM AND PRACTICE BY ASKING YOURSELF DIFFERENT WAYS TO SLIGHTLY CHANGE THE QUESTION BC THATS WHAT HIS TESTS ARE.

Dr. Wilhite's tests are ACTUALLY fair and straightforward, unlike many other professor's tests in the dept. It's not easy material, so the lectures can be hard to follow along, but this is pretty standard in the chen dept. Dr. Wilhite's quirky sense of humor makes lecture entertaining, and he is not a harsh grader. TAKE HIM. Non-cumulative final.

He's a real good choice for a prof. My only complaints are the errors in his presentation slides. Often times equations were wrong or formatted in a way that was ambiguous. However, this can be avoided by just following the equations found in the book, so it's not that big of a deal. I wouldn't call his class easy, but it's doable.

Lectures were almost always outstanding, knows a lot more material than what is in the textbook. Not very helpful in office hours though, did not answer questions outside of class. Gives test reviews that are very helpful for exams.  Tough grader, gives no partial credit. Very funny in class, has a great sense of humor. Challenging but worth it.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Makes awesome Firesign Theater references, like "Fudd's First Law of Opposition," and totally knows his old-school references to 70's songs.
